101.summary: Break numbers into prime factors to find highest common factors and lowest common multiples quickly.
key_concepts: Every integer above 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way
HCF uses the lowest power of each shared prime
LCM uses the highest power of every prime that appears

formulas.note: Useful when you already know three of the four values.
formulas.label: Product of two numbers
formulas.expression: a x b = HCF(a, b) x LCM(a, b)

steps: HCF: lowest powers of shared primes = 2^2 x 3 = 12
LCM: highest power of every prime = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 x 7 = 2520
worked_examples.question: Find the HCF and LCM of 84 and 360.

common_mistakes.fix: That only works when the HCF is 1. Otherwise divide the product by the HCF.
common_mistakes.mistake: Multiplying the two numbers together to get the LCM.

common_mistakes.fix: The HCF uses shared primes only.
common_mistakes.mistake: Including primes that appear in only one number when finding the HCF.

exam_tips: Write prime factorisations in index form before comparing them.
Smallest number divisible by both is asking for an LCM.

102.summary: Index laws let you simplify powers without expanding, and standard form keeps very large or small numbers manageable.
key_concepts: Add indices when multiplying, subtract when dividing
A negative index means a reciprocal
Standard form is A x 10^n where 1 <= A < 10

formulas.note: Bases must be the same.
formulas.label: Multiplying powers

formulas.note: Never makes the answer negative.
formulas.label: Negative index

formulas.note: Denominator is the root, numerator is the power.
formulas.label: Fractional index

steps: Subtract powers of a: a^(5-2) = a^3
Subtract powers of b: b^(2-1) = b
worked_examples.question: Simplify 6a^5b^2 divided by 3a^2b.

common_mistakes.fix: A negative index flips the base into a fraction. It does not change the sign.
common_mistakes.mistake: Writing a^(-2) as a negative number.

common_mistakes.fix: The first part must be between 1 and 10, so write 3.4 x 10^6.
common_mistakes.mistake: Leaving standard form as 34 x 10^5.

exam_tips: Simplify numbers and each letter separately, one at a time.
Check the standard form range before writing your final answer.

202.summary: In direct proportion one quantity is a constant multiple of the other. In inverse proportion their product is constant.
key_concepts: Direct proportion graphs are straight lines through the origin
Find the constant k using the given pair of values first
Inverse proportion means y increases as x decreases

formulas.note: y is proportional to x.
formulas.label: Direct proportion

formulas.note: Also written as xy = k.
formulas.label: Inverse proportion

steps: Substitute: 1 = k x cube root of 8 = 2k, so k = 1/2
When x = 124: y = 1/2 x cube root of 125 = 1/2 x 5
worked_examples.question: y is directly proportional to the cube root of (x + 1), and y = 1 when x = 7. Find y when x = 124.

common_mistakes.fix: Always substitute the given pair to find k before answering.
common_mistakes.mistake: Skipping the step of finding k.

common_mistakes.fix: Inverse proportion is y = k/x. Read the wording carefully.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using y = kx when the question says inversely proportional.

exam_tips: Underline whether the question says directly or inversely proportional.
If d is halved in an inverse square relation, F becomes four times larger.

204.summary: A scale compares drawing length to actual length. Areas scale by the square of the length scale.
key_concepts: A scale of 1 : n means 1 unit on the map represents n of the same units in reality
Convert both lengths to the same unit before writing a scale
If lengths scale by 1 : n, then areas scale by 1 : n squared
A scale has no units because both sides are the same measure

formulas.note: Both sides must be in the same unit.
formulas.label: Length scale

formulas.note: Square the length scale factor to get the area scale.
formulas.label: Area scale

steps: 1 cm on the map represents 50000 cm = 0.5 km
worked_examples.question: A map has scale 1 : 50000. A park covers 8 cm^2 on the map. Find its actual area in km^2.

common_mistakes.fix: Square it. Areas scale by n squared, not by n.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using the length scale factor directly for an area.

common_mistakes.fix: Convert both lengths to the same unit, then simplify to the form 1 : n.
common_mistakes.mistake: Writing a scale without converting units first.

exam_tips: Convert the length scale into a convenient unit such as km before working with areas.
Check whether the question asks for a length or an area, that decides whether you square.

301.summary: Percentage questions almost always come down to identifying which value counts as 100 percent.
key_concepts: The original value is always the 100 percent baseline
A multiplier is faster and safer than working out the change separately
Reverse percentage means dividing by the multiplier, not multiplying

formulas.note: Original is the value before the change.
formulas.label: Percentage change

formulas.note: For a decrease use (1 - rate/100).
formulas.label: Increase multiplier

steps: A 24 percent loss means $136 is 76 percent of the cost price
Keep the full value in your calculator, do not round yet
worked_examples.question: A shopkeeper makes a 24 percent loss selling an item for $136. Find the selling price needed for a 40 percent profit instead.

common_mistakes.fix: Divide by 0.76. Reverse percentages divide by the multiplier.
common_mistakes.mistake: Multiplying by 1.24 to reverse a 24 percent loss.

common_mistakes.fix: Percentage change is always measured against the original.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using the new value as the 100 percent baseline.

exam_tips: Write down what represents 100 percent before calculating anything.
Keep full accuracy in working and round only at the end.

302.summary: Simple interest is a fixed amount each year. Compound interest grows on the new balance each year.
key_concepts: Simple interest is linear, compound interest is exponential
Compound interest formula gives the total amount, not the interest
Subtract the principal to get the interest earned

formulas.note: P is principal, R is percent per year, T is years.
formulas.label: Simple interest
formulas.expression: I = P x R x T / 100

formulas.note: A is the final amount. Interest earned = A - P.
formulas.label: Compound amount

steps: Take the 10th root of both sides: 1 + r/100 = 1.0260
worked_examples.question: Jessica invests $4540 at r percent compound interest per year. After 10 years she has earned $1328.54 in interest. Find r.

common_mistakes.fix: Interest earned = final amount minus the principal.
common_mistakes.mistake: Reporting the compound amount when the question asks for the interest.

common_mistakes.fix: Compound interest recalculates on the new balance each period.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using simple interest when the question says compound.

exam_tips: Check whether the question wants the total amount or just the interest.
For an unknown rate, take the nth root of both sides.

303.subtopic_name: Exchange rates, hire purchase and taxation
303.summary: Everyday finance: converting currency, buying by instalments, and working out tax charged in bands.
key_concepts: Check the size of a converted amount to confirm you multiplied the right way
A hire purchase total is the deposit plus every instalment, and always exceeds the cash price
Tax is charged in bands, so only the income inside each band is taxed at that band's rate

formulas.note: The amount above the cash price is the interest charged.
formulas.label: Hire purchase total
formulas.expression: total = deposit + (number of instalments x instalment amount)

formulas.note: Use the rate in the direction you need, or divide by the reverse rate.
formulas.label: Currency conversion
formulas.expression: new amount = original amount x rate

worked_examples.question: A laptop costs $1200 cash, or a $300 deposit plus 12 monthly payments of $82. How much extra does the instalment plan cost?

steps: Each Singapore dollar is worth 0.75 US dollars
worked_examples.question: If S$1 = US$0.75, convert S$300 into US dollars.

common_mistakes.fix: Sanity-check the size. Converting into a weaker currency should give a larger number.
common_mistakes.mistake: Multiplying when you should divide in a currency conversion.

common_mistakes.fix: Total = deposit + all instalments.
common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting the deposit when totalling a hire purchase plan.

common_mistakes.fix: Only the part of the income inside a band is taxed at that band's rate.
common_mistakes.mistake: Taxing the whole income at the highest band rate.

exam_tips: Write the exchange rate as a fraction and check which unit cancels.
Hire purchase always costs more than cash, so use that to check your answer.

401.summary: Expanding removes brackets, factorising puts them back. Most algebra marks come from doing these two accurately.
key_concepts: Every term inside the bracket must be multiplied
Always take out the highest common factor first
For a quadratic, find two numbers with the right product and sum

formulas.note: Spot this whenever there is no middle term.
formulas.label: Difference of two squares

formulas.note: The middle term is twice the product.
formulas.label: Perfect square

steps: Need two numbers with product 20 and sum -9
worked_examples.question: Factorise completely x^2 - 9x + 20.

common_mistakes.fix: You must include the 2ab middle term.
common_mistakes.mistake: Writing (a + b)^2 as a^2 + b^2.

common_mistakes.fix: Check whether the remaining bracket factorises further.
common_mistakes.mistake: Stopping after one factor when the question says completely.

exam_tips: Expand your factorised answer mentally to check it.
Completely is a hint that there are at least two stages.

402.subtopic_name: Algebraic fractions and changing the subject
402.summary: Combine algebraic fractions over a common denominator, and rearrange formulas by undoing operations in reverse order.
key_concepts: Factorise every denominator before finding the common denominator
Only cancel factors, never individual terms
To change the subject, collect all terms with that letter on one side

formulas.note: Simplify the result if possible.
formulas.label: Adding fractions

worked_examples.question: Write 3/(x + 2) + 1/(x - 2) as a single fraction.

common_mistakes.fix: You can only cancel a factor common to the whole numerator and denominator.
common_mistakes.mistake: Cancelling the x in (x + 3)/x.

common_mistakes.fix: Moving a term to the other side reverses its sign.
common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting to change signs when moving a term across the equals sign.

exam_tips: Never cancel across a plus or minus sign.
When the new subject appears twice, factorise it out.

501.summary: Every straight line can be written as y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c the y-intercept.
key_concepts: Gradient measures how steep the line is
Parallel lines share the same gradient
A negative gradient slopes downwards from left to right

formulas.note: Keep the order of subtraction consistent.
formulas.label: Gradient from two points

formulas.note: c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
formulas.label: Equation of a line

worked_examples.question: Find the equation of the line through (1, 5) and (3, 11).

common_mistakes.fix: Gradient is change in y over change in x.
common_mistakes.mistake: Computing the gradient as change in x over change in y.

common_mistakes.fix: If you start with point 2 on top, start with point 2 on the bottom too.
common_mistakes.mistake: Mixing up the order of the points in the numerator and denominator.

exam_tips: Sketch the two points quickly to check whether the gradient should be positive or negative.
Read the axis scales before measuring a gradient off a graph.

502.summary: Recognising the shape of a graph from its equation saves time and prevents sketching errors.
key_concepts: A positive x^2 coefficient gives a U shape, a negative one gives an n shape
The turning point is the minimum or maximum of a quadratic
Completing the square reveals the turning point directly

formulas.note: The turning point is at (a, b).
formulas.label: Completed square form

formulas.note: A hyperbola with the axes as asymptotes.
formulas.label: Reciprocal graph

steps: Half of -10 is -5, so start with (x - 5)^2
The squared term is smallest (zero) when x = 5
worked_examples.question: Write x^2 - 10x + 7 in the form (x - a)^2 + b and state the minimum value.

common_mistakes.fix: The x-coordinate is +5. The sign inside the bracket flips.
common_mistakes.mistake: Reading the turning point of (x - 5)^2 - 18 as (-5, -18).

common_mistakes.fix: Draw a single smooth curve through the points.
common_mistakes.mistake: Joining plotted points with straight lines.

exam_tips: Identify the shape from the equation before plotting anything.
The minimum of a squared term is always zero, which fixes the turning point.

601.summary: Solve inequalities exactly like equations, with one extra rule about multiplying or dividing by a negative.
key_concepts: Do the same operation to both sides to stay balanced
Multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the inequality sign
Integer solutions must be listed, not just described

formulas.note: Dividing by -1 flips the inequality.
formulas.label: Sign reversal rule

worked_examples.question: Find the first negative term of the sequence whose nth term is 87 - 9n.

common_mistakes.fix: Reverse the sign whenever you multiply or divide by a negative number.
common_mistakes.mistake: Keeping the inequality sign the same after dividing by a negative.

common_mistakes.fix: Round to the correct integer and check it satisfies the inequality.
common_mistakes.mistake: Giving n > 9.67 as the final answer for an integer question.

exam_tips: After solving, test one value from your range to confirm it works.
On a number line, use an open circle for < and a filled circle for <=.

602.summary: Two unknowns need two equations. Quadratics need factorising, the formula, or completing the square.
key_concepts: Elimination works well when coefficients match, substitution when one variable is isolated
A quadratic must equal zero before you factorise it
The discriminant tells you how many real roots there are

formulas.note: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0.
formulas.label: Quadratic formula

formulas.note: Positive gives 2 roots, zero gives 1, negative gives none.
formulas.label: Discriminant

steps: The y terms are +2y and -2y, so adding the equations eliminates y
worked_examples.question: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 16 and x - 2y = 0.

steps: Already equal to zero, so try factorising
Two numbers with product 2 x (-3) = -6 and sum -5 are -6 and +1
worked_examples.question: Solve 2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0.

common_mistakes.fix: Move every term to one side so the equation reads ... = 0 first.
common_mistakes.mistake: Trying to factorise a quadratic that has not been rearranged to equal zero.

common_mistakes.fix: A quadratic usually has two solutions. State both.
common_mistakes.mistake: Giving only one solution to a quadratic.

common_mistakes.fix: Opposite signs means add to eliminate. Matching signs means subtract.
common_mistakes.mistake: Subtracting the simultaneous equations when the signs are already opposite.

exam_tips: Substitute both answers back into the original equation to check.
If the question says give answers to 2 decimal places, it wants the formula, not factorising.

701.summary: Sets group objects. Most marks come from reading the notation correctly and shading the right region.
key_concepts: Union means everything in either set, intersection means only what is in both
The complement is everything in the universal set that is not in the set
n(A) means the number of elements in A

formulas.note: Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.
formulas.label: Union count
formulas.expression: n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersect B)

formulas.note: The prime symbol means not in A.
formulas.label: Complement

steps: No element is in both, so the intersection is empty
worked_examples.question: The universal set is the integers 1 to 15. A is the perfect squares and B is the primes. Find n(A union B).

common_mistakes.fix: Elements in both sets would be counted twice. Subtract the intersection.
common_mistakes.mistake: Adding n(A) and n(B) without subtracting the overlap.

common_mistakes.fix: Union looks like a cup and collects everything. Intersection is the overlap only.
common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing the union and intersection symbols.

exam_tips: Always list the actual elements before counting them.
Fill the intersection of a Venn diagram first, then work outwards.

801.summary: Matrices store data in rows and columns. Order matters for multiplication, and the dimensions must match.
key_concepts: You can only add or subtract matrices of the same size
For multiplication, the columns of the first must equal the rows of the second
AB is usually not the same as BA

formulas.note: Always state rows first, then columns.
formulas.label: Order of a matrix

formulas.note: The inner numbers must match; the outer numbers give the size of the answer.
formulas.label: Multiplication dimensions
formulas.expression: (m x n) x (n x p) = (m x p)

formulas.note: Every entry is multiplied by k.
formulas.label: Scalar multiplication
formulas.expression: k x (a b / c d) = (ka kb / kc kd)

steps: Each row of the recipe matrix is one ingredient
Each entry of the cakes matrix is how many of that cake are made
Multiplying sums ingredient amount times cake count
worked_examples.answer: Each element is the total amount of one ingredient needed for all the cakes.
worked_examples.question: A recipe matrix is multiplied by a number-of-cakes matrix. Explain what the product elements represent.

common_mistakes.fix: Multiply each row of the first matrix by each column of the second, then add.
common_mistakes.mistake: Multiplying matrices element by element.

common_mistakes.fix: Matrix multiplication is not commutative. Keep the given order.
common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming AB equals BA.

exam_tips: Write the dimensions above each matrix before multiplying to check it is possible.
For interpretation questions, state what a row and a column represent in context.

1001.summary: Congruent figures are identical in size and shape. Similar figures have the same shape with all lengths scaled by one factor.
key_concepts: Congruence tests are SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS
Similar shapes have equal corresponding angles and a constant ratio of sides
Area and volume scale by the square and cube of the length scale factor

formulas.note: Match the corresponding sides carefully.
formulas.label: Length scale factor
formulas.expression: k = corresponding length on B / corresponding length on A

formulas.note: A very common source of lost marks.
formulas.label: Area and volume scaling
formulas.expression: area ratio = k^2, volume ratio = k^3

worked_examples.question: Two similar solids have heights 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller has volume 32 cm^3. Find the volume of the larger.

common_mistakes.fix: Square it for area and cube it for volume.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using the length scale factor directly for area or volume.

common_mistakes.fix: Match sides by the equal angles they sit between.
common_mistakes.mistake: Pairing sides that do not correspond.

exam_tips: Sketch both shapes the same way round before pairing sides.
For congruence proofs, state the test abbreviation such as SAS explicitly.

1201.summary: In a right-angled triangle, use Pythagoras for sides only and SOHCAHTOA when an angle is involved.
key_concepts: The hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle
Label the sides opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to the angle you are using
Use the inverse function to find an angle from two sides

formulas.note: c is the hypotenuse. Rearrange to find a shorter side.
formulas.label: Pythagoras theorem

formulas.note: Choose the ratio that uses the two sides you know.
formulas.label: SOHCAHTOA
formulas.expression: sin = O/H, cos = A/H, tan = O/A

worked_examples.question: A ladder 5 m long leans against a wall with its foot 1.4 m from the base. Find the angle with the ground.

common_mistakes.fix: Pythagoras only relates three sides. Use trigonometry when an angle appears.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using Pythagoras when one of the given values is an angle.

common_mistakes.fix: Set the calculator to degrees before any trigonometry.
common_mistakes.mistake: Leaving the calculator in radian mode.

exam_tips: Label the three sides relative to your chosen angle before picking a ratio.
Check the hypotenuse is the longest side in your answer.

1401.summary: Gradient, midpoint and distance are three formulas that answer nearly every coordinate question.
key_concepts: Midpoint is the average of the coordinates
Perpendicular gradients multiply to give -1
Distance between points comes straight from Pythagoras

formulas.note: Average each coordinate separately.
formulas.label: Midpoint

formulas.note: Pythagoras applied to the coordinate differences.
formulas.label: Distance

formulas.note: The perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal.
formulas.label: Perpendicular gradient

steps: Original gradient is 2, so perpendicular gradient is -1/2
worked_examples.question: Find the equation of the line perpendicular to y = 2x + 1 passing through (4, 3).

common_mistakes.fix: Take the negative reciprocal, which is -1/2, not just the negative.
common_mistakes.mistake: Using -2 as the perpendicular gradient to 2.

common_mistakes.fix: Midpoint means average, so add and divide by two.
common_mistakes.mistake: Subtracting coordinates when finding a midpoint.

exam_tips: Plot the points roughly to sanity-check your answer.
Perpendicular gradient means flip the fraction and change the sign.

1501.summary: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Route-finding through a diagram is the core skill.
key_concepts: Vector AB means go from A to B, and BA is its negative
Add vectors by following one route then another
Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other

formulas.note: For the column vector with components x and y.
formulas.label: Magnitude

formulas.note: Any route from A to B gives the same vector.
formulas.label: Route addition

steps: Travel from A back to O, then O to B
worked_examples.question: OA is vector a and OB is vector b. Express AB in terms of a and b.

common_mistakes.fix: AB = b - a. You subtract the start point from the end point.
common_mistakes.mistake: Writing AB as a - b.

common_mistakes.fix: Add the components first, then apply the magnitude formula.
common_mistakes.mistake: Adding the magnitudes of two vectors to get the magnitude of their sum.

exam_tips: Draw arrows on the diagram for every vector you write down.
If two vectors are parallel, write one as k times the other and solve for k.

1601.summary: Mean, median and mode each summarise data differently, and the range or interquartile range describes the spread.
key_concepts: The median needs the data ordered first
The mean is affected by extreme values, the median is not
Interquartile range describes the middle half of the data

formulas.note: x is the value, f is its frequency.
formulas.label: Mean from a frequency table
formulas.expression: mean = sum of (fx) / sum of f

formulas.note: Ignores extreme values at both ends.
formulas.label: Interquartile range

worked_examples.question: A cumulative frequency graph for 200 students gives a lower quartile of 59 marks and an upper quartile of 77 marks. Find the interquartile range.

common_mistakes.fix: Always sort the values into order first.
common_mistakes.mistake: Finding the median without ordering the data.

common_mistakes.fix: The median is read at half the total frequency on the vertical axis.
common_mistakes.mistake: Reading the median at the halfway point of the marks axis.

exam_tips: If a question mentions outliers, the median and IQR are usually the better measures.
State units with every average and spread you calculate.

1602.subtopic_name: Standard deviation and comparing data sets
1602.summary: Standard deviation measures how spread out data is around the mean. Use it alongside the mean to compare two sets.
key_concepts: A larger standard deviation means the data is more spread out and less consistent
Compare two data sets by commenting on the average and on the spread separately
Standard deviation uses every value, so extreme values affect it
Always give the comparison in the context of the question

formulas.note: Work out the mean and the mean of the squares first.
formulas.label: Standard deviation

formulas.note: From a frequency table, use sum of fx divided by sum of f.
formulas.label: Mean

worked_examples.answer: Mean 7 and standard deviation 1.90 to 3 significant figures
worked_examples.question: Five students score 4, 6, 7, 9 and 9. Find the mean and the standard deviation.

common_mistakes.fix: It is the mean of the squares minus the square of the mean. That result is never negative.
common_mistakes.mistake: Subtracting in the wrong order inside the square root.

common_mistakes.fix: Mention both the average and the spread to earn full marks.
common_mistakes.mistake: Comparing two data sets using the mean alone.

common_mistakes.fix: Standard deviation uses every value; the range uses only the two extremes.
common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing standard deviation with the range or interquartile range.

exam_tips: Set out a table of x and x squared before substituting into the formula.
A smaller standard deviation means more consistent, which is usually the point of the comparison.

1603.subtopic_name: Statistical diagrams and cumulative frequency curves
1603.summary: Different diagrams suit different data. A cumulative frequency curve gives the median and quartiles by reading across and down.
key_concepts: A cumulative frequency curve plots the running total against the upper class boundary
Read the median at half the total frequency on the vertical axis, then across to the curve and down
Quartiles are read at one quarter and three quarters of the total frequency
A box-and-whisker plot shows the minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum

formulas.note: n is the total frequency.
formulas.label: Median position
formulas.expression: read across at n / 2 on the cumulative frequency axis

formulas.note: Always read across from the vertical axis first.
formulas.label: Quartile positions
formulas.expression: lower quartile at n / 4, upper quartile at 3n / 4

formulas.note: Describes the spread of the middle half of the data.
formulas.label: Interquartile range

steps: For the median, read across from 100 on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then down to the marks axis
For scores above 70, read up from 70 to the curve to find how many scored 70 or less
worked_examples.answer: The median is read at a cumulative frequency of 100, and the number above 70 marks is 200 minus the curve reading at 70
worked_examples.question: A cumulative frequency curve covers 200 students. Explain how to find the median, and how many scored more than 70 marks.

common_mistakes.fix: The median is read at half the total frequency on the vertical axis, not halfway along the horizontal axis.
common_mistakes.mistake: Reading the median halfway along the marks axis.

common_mistakes.fix: Plot it against the upper class boundary.
common_mistakes.mistake: Plotting cumulative frequency against the class midpoint.

common_mistakes.fix: Subtract the reading from the total frequency.
common_mistakes.mistake: Giving the curve reading as the answer when asked how many scored more than a value.

exam_tips: Draw your reading lines onto the graph, they show the examiner your method.
Check your curve finishes at the total frequency.
